The Contraction Cobweb

A cobweb spirals into a single point. That point is the fixed point.

Repeatedly apply a map that shrinks distances by a fixed ratio. The points crowd closer and closer together. In the end only one point can remain.

For example, nest a smaller 📦 box inside a box, then a smaller one inside that, and the boxes close in on a single point. Each step leaves less room than the last.

d(f(x),f(y))≤q d(x,y),  q<1  ⇒  xn+1=f(xn)→x∗d(f(x),f(y)) \le q\,d(x,y),\; q<1 \;\Rightarrow\; x_{n+1} = f(x_n) \to x^*d(f(x),f(y))≤qd(x,y),q<1⇒xn+1​=f(xn​)→x∗

    Since ξ∈[0,1]⊂[0,π2)\xi \in [0,1] \subset [0, \frac{\pi}{2})ξ∈[0,1]⊂[0,2π​) and sin⁡\sinsin is increasing on [0,π2)[0, \frac{\pi}{2})[0,2π​), ∣sin⁡ξ∣≤sin⁡(1)|\sin\xi| \le \sin(1)∣sinξ∣≤sin(1), so ∣cos⁡x−cos⁡y∣≤sin⁡(1) ∣x−y∣|\cos x - \cos y| \le \sin(1)\,|x - y|∣cosx−cosy∣≤sin(1)∣x−y∣, and sin⁡(1)≈0.8415<1\sin(1) \approx 0.8415 < 1sin(1)≈0.8415<1, so cos⁡\coscos is a contraction.

Prove in three lines that there is at most one fixed point.

∣x∗−y∗∣=∣f(x∗)−f(y∗)∣≤q∣x∗−y∗∣|x^* - y^*| = |f(x^*) - f(y^*)| \le q|x^* - y^*|∣x∗−y∗∣=∣f(x∗)−f(y∗)∣≤q∣x∗−y∗∣
Show proof

  1. Suppose x∗x^*x∗ and y∗y^*y∗ are both fixed points.

  2. Then ∣x∗−y∗∣=∣f(x∗)−f(y∗)∣≤q∣x∗−y∗∣|x^* - y^*| = |f(x^*) - f(y^*)| \le q|x^* - y^*|∣x∗−y∗∣=∣f(x∗)−f(y∗)∣≤q∣x∗−y∗∣.

  3. Since q<1q < 1q<1, this forces ∣x∗−y∗∣=0|x^* - y^*| = 0∣x∗−y∗∣=0, i.e. x∗=y∗x^* = y^*x∗=y∗.
